subject: Social Habits
title: Classroom routines
objectives: Children will follow simple classroom routines.
Children will help to tidy up when asked.
content: Circle time and listening, lining up and walking, and tidy-up time.
teachingActivities: Use the same routine words and songs every day; show before you tell; give a warning before change; praise children who follow the routine; keep each routine short; let children have jobs.
learnerActivities: Follow simple classroom routines such as sitting in the circle, lining up and tidying.
resources: A line of footprints on the floor
assessment: Observe whether each child sits in the circle, joins a line and helps to tidy with support.
expectedOutcomes: Sits in the circle and joins a line with support.
crossCurricular: Physical Development: walking in a line

lessons.title: Circle time
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will sit in the circle and listen for a short time.
successCriteria: Sits on the mat for two minutes
Looks at the teacher when called
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet, use please and thank you and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Sing "Come and sit, come and sit, sit in the circle" and show where to sit.
teacherActivities: Show how to sit on the mat with a quiet body.
Say "Listening ears on" and touch your ears.
Tell a very short story with the puppet.
learnerActivities: Children touch their ears and look.
Children stay seated for a short time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to sit on the mat with a quiet body. Children: Children sit and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Listening ears on" and touch your ears. Children: Children touch their ears and look.
Step 3. Teacher: Tell a very short story with the puppet. Children: Children listen and smile.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise children who sit well. Children: Children stay seated for a short time.

practical.title: Circle time practice
practical.safety: Leave space between children and sit away from furniture. Never force a child to sit; offer a lap or a quiet spot.

differentiation.support: Sit beside the child and use a short time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help a friend find a place.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we use to listen?

expectedOutcomes: Sits in the circle for a short time
Looks at the teacher when called
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and stand up quietly.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise sitting together for a short story at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sit in the circle and listen for a short time" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Come and sit, come and sit, sit in the circle.

lessons.title: Lining up and walking
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will line up and walk with the group.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet, use please and thank you and name feelings.
resources: A rope with loops or a hand-hold
lessons.starter: Put footprints on the floor and say "Let us stand on the footprints and make a line."
teacherActivities: Show how to stand on a footprint.
Say "Walk, walk, walk" and lead the line.
Stop and start with a signal.
Walk to the door and back.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to stand on a footprint. Children: Children stand on footprints.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Walk, walk, walk" and lead the line. Children: Children walk in a line.
Step 3. Teacher: Stop and start with a signal. Children: Children stop and wait.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk to the door and back. Children: Children walk with a friend.

practical.title: Line and walk
practical.safety: Keep the route clear of hazards and keep children at a walking pace. An adult must be at the front and the back of the line.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand at the front of the line.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the line leader.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the signal?

expectedOutcomes: Walks and stops on a signal
lessons.conclusion: Sing the line-up song and sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise walking holding hands at home and outside.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "line up and walk with the group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tidy-up time
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will help to put toys away when the tidy-up song plays.
successCriteria: Puts a toy in a basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet, use please and thank you and name feelings.
resources: Toys with pictures on the baskets
lessons.starter: Sing "Tidy up, tidy up, everybody tidy up" and point to the toys on the floor.
teacherActivities: Show how to put a block in the block basket.
Sing the tidy-up song while children work.
Check the floor together and say "All tidy."
learnerActivities: Child looks at the floor and says tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put a block in the block basket. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the tidy-up song while children work. Children: Children put toys in baskets.
Step 3. Teacher: Check the floor together and say "All tidy." Children: Child looks at the floor and says tidy.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise the tidy room. Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Tidy up
steps: Look at the toys on the floor.
practical.safety: Keep walkways clear and supervise lifting of large items. Use large, light toys only.

differentiation.support: Tidy together and name each toy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend where a toy goes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says tidy up with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Look at the tidy room and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a small tidying job at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help to put toys away when the tidy-up song plays" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Tidy up, tidy up, everybody tidy up.

lessons.title: Our daily routine
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will follow the picture timetable and know what comes next.
successCriteria: Moves to the next activity with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet, use please and thank you and name feelings.
resources: A picture timetable with four to six pictures
lessons.starter: Show the picture timetable and say "First circle, then play, then snack, then home."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say what happens.
Ring the bell and move to the next picture.
Let a child turn over a picture to show what is next.
Talk about how routines help us feel safe.
learnerActivities: Children look and name the activity.
Children move to the next activity.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say what happens. Children: Children look and name the activity.
Step 2. Teacher: Ring the bell and move to the next picture. Children: Children move to the next activity.
Step 3. Teacher: Let a child turn over a picture to show what is next. Children: Child turns the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about how routines help us feel safe. Children: Children smile and nod.

practical.title: Following the timetable
practical.safety: Keep transitions calm and give a warning before changes. Stay near children who find change hard.

differentiation.support: Point to the picture and walk with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell what comes after snack.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do after play?

expectedOutcomes: Moves to the next activity with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Use a simple picture routine at home for morning and bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "follow the picture timetable and know what comes next" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 routines check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child follows routines.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can greet, use please and thank you and name feelings.
lessons.starter: Sing the circle song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: circle, line and tidy.
At each station watch how the child follows the routine.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: circle, line and tidy. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child follows the routine. Children: Child follows with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Routine stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep walkways clear. Use light, large objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one routine.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead the line.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sits for circle time; joins a line; helps to tidy; follows the picture timetable.

questions.question: What do we do with toys?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using simple routines at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child follows routines" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
